purpose: Phase 9 Step 10 - rate limiter correctness audit using an injectable fake clock (monkeypatched time.time/time.sleep inside utils.rate_limiter), per the governing directive's requirement to avoid real sleeps.
generated_from: tests/test_phase9_rate_limiter_audit.py (15 tests, all PASS at generation time)
module_under_test: utils/rate_limiter.py (TokenBucket, RateLimiter, wait_for_rate_limit) - read in full this pass, unmodified

first_request_behavior.description: First call against a fresh bucket at any tested provider rate never waits (bucket starts at full capacity, capacity>=1 required and confirmed present for the sub-1/s NVIDIA/Cerebras rates).

subsequent_request_spacing.pubmed_3rps_burst_then_wait: first 3 calls free (capacity=3), 4th call waits - confirmed

independent_buckets_per_key.description: Exhausting one provider's bucket (e.g. pubmed) has zero effect on another's (e.g. chembl) - confirmed via a shared RateLimiter instance with 2 distinct keys.

simultaneous_callers.description: 5 real threads racing threading.Barrier-synchronized calls against a capacity=1 bucket: at most 1 consumed the pre-existing token without waiting; the rest genuinely waited (observed via sleep_calls growth). Directly at the TokenBucket.consume() level, 10 racing threads against a 1-token bucket produced EXACTLY 1 successful consume(), never 0, never >1 - the internal threading.Lock in TokenBucket.consume() prevents double-spending the same token.

queue_wait_behavior.description: wait_for_token() is a plain spin-wait loop (while not consume(): time.sleep(0.1)), confirmed via source reading and via test_wait_for_token_blocks_until_available_deterministically in the pre-existing tests/test_rate_limiter.py. No FIFO queue exists - RateLimiter/TokenBucket expose no queue primitive (confirmed via hasattr checks).

fairness.verdict: not guaranteed by design - documented, not asserted as a bug
fairness.description: Because wait_for_token() is an unordered spin-wait with no queue, under contention the thread whose consume() call happens to run first after a refill wins, not necessarily the thread that arrived first. This is an inherent property of the polling design, not a defect this audit found freshly - not measured further (would require statistical fairness measurement across many contended refills, out of this pass's scope, and not something the exit gate asks for).

retry_interaction.verdict: confirmed: every retry attempt consumes its own token
retry_interaction.description: wait_for_rate_limit() is called BEFORE the HTTP/LLM attempt at every real call site (candidate_b_native_tools.py, config/llm_config.py, grounding_eval/judge.py, generation/generator.py) and has no visibility into whether that attempt succeeds or fails - it unconditionally gates and consumes a token per call, including every retry attempt. Confirmed empirically: 3 consecutive wait() calls (simulating LLM_CALL_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3) against a capacity=1, 1/s bucket produced >=2 waits (1 free + 2 forced waits) - i.e. failed attempts DO consume a rate-limit token/slot, they are not free/exempted.
retry_interaction.implication: This means a burst of retries (e.g. 3 NVIDIA-client retry attempts after a 503) counts as 3 separate rate-limited calls against the 35 RPM bucket, not 1 - already accounted for in config/llm_config.py's own documented rationale for capping at 35 rather than the true 40 RPM limit ("a burst of retries after a transient 503 could otherwise tip a run over the hard limit").

burst_bound.verdict: PASS - no burst above configured capacity observed
burst_bound.description: A TokenBucket never allows more than `capacity` tokens' worth of consumption without an intervening wait, regardless of call pattern (rapid-fire consume() calls tested directly).

provider_instance_correctness.description: Each of the 5 real provider/source keys (nvidia_nim_llm, cerebras_candidate_b_native_tools/cerebras_free_trial, pubmed, clinical_trials, chembl) is a distinct RateLimiter bucket key, confirmed via RateLimiter.get_bucket's key-to-bucket dict and the independent-buckets test above - no cross-provider bucket sharing found in the codebase.

inefficiencies_noted_not_defects: wait_for_token()'s 0.1s spin-wait polling is CPU-cheap but adds up to 0.1s of avoidable wait latency per refill-wait event versus an event-driven wake mechanism - a performance, not correctness, observation, and explicitly out of scope to fix (no optimization permitted this pass).

No fairness/ordering guarantee under contention - acceptable for this codebase's actual usage pattern (single-process, a handful of concurrent tasks) but would need revisiting only if a fairness-sensitive multi-tenant scenario were introduced (Phase 10+ territory, not measured here).
